s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute onset of pain and swelling around the scapula and ankle with systemic symptoms
salient_findings: Pain and swelling around the right scapula
Swelling and pain of the left ankle
Fever
Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein level
Magnetic resonance imaging findings consistent with osteomyelitis
key_facts: 18-year-old man
20 days of pain and swelling around the right scapula
2 days of fever
Receiving anti-tubercular therapy for 6 months
Diagnosis of presumed pulmonary tuberculosis based on cough, chest radiograph findings, and elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate
Negative sputum studies
Swelling and pain of the left ankle with difficulty walking
Erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 73 mm/h
Positive C-reactive protein level of 96 mg/L
Magnetic resonance imaging findings consistent with osteomyelitis involving the scapula and the distal tibia

shortlist.label: Tuberculous osteomyelitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is receiving anti-tubercular therapy and has findings consistent with osteomyelitis, suggesting possible spread of tuberculosis to the bones

shortlist.label: Chronic osteomyelitis
shortlist.why_kept: Magnetic resonance imaging findings consistent with osteomyelitis involving the scapula and the distal tibia, and patient has been experiencing pain and swelling for 20 days

shortlist.label: Bacterial osteomyelitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has systemic symptoms such as fever and elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate, which could indicate a bacterial infection

shortlist.label: Multidrug-resistant tuberculosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has been receiving anti-tubercular therapy for 6 months but still has active disease, raising the possibility of multidrug-resistant tuberculosis

shortlist.label: Chronic recurrent multifocal osteomyelitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has multiple sites of osteomyelitis and a prolonged course of disease, which could suggest a chronic recurrent condition
